title: New Zealand's North Island
subtitle: Hawke's Bay and Martinborough
objectives: Describe Hawke's Bay and Gimblett Gravels

steps.title: A maritime country
steps.body: New Zealand's two islands stretch from about 36 to 46 degrees south, and no vineyard is far from the sea. The climate is cool and maritime, with high sunlight and strong ultraviolet levels. Rain can come at harvest, so site and vintage matter. Sauvignon Blanc is over 60% of production.

steps.title: Hawke's Bay
steps.body: Hawke's Bay, on the North Island's east coast, is New Zealand's second largest region and one of its warmest. Gimblett Gravels, an old riverbed of stony soils, stores heat and drains well. It makes Bordeaux blends and Syrah. Chardonnay is also important.
steps.highlight: Gimblett Gravels: Bordeaux blends and Syrah

steps.prompt: What makes Gimblett Gravels good for red grapes?
options: Stony soils that store heat and drain well
steps.explanation: Old riverbed gravel stores warmth and drains, helping red grapes ripen.

steps.title: Martinborough
steps.body: Martinborough, in the Wairarapa near Wellington, is small, dry and windy. In the 1980s, scientists identified its climate and soils as similar to Burgundy's. Its Pinot Noir is concentrated and savoury. Strong winds lower yields but keep grapes healthy.

steps.prompt: Sauvignon Blanc makes up over 60% of New Zealand's production.
steps.explanation: Yes. It dominates exports, though Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are growing.

steps.title: What you learned
points: New Zealand is cool, maritime and bright
Hawke's Bay's Gimblett Gravels makes Bordeaux blends and Syrah
